passage:
A new tunnel shortened the road between two towns. Drivers were happy because the trip became twenty minutes faster.
However, shops along the old mountain road lost customers. Some closed within months. Hikers also complained that fewer people cared for the old path.
The local government promoted the old road as a slow travel route, with signs for viewpoints, history stops, and small restaurants.
The tunnel solved one problem but created others.
Infrastructure changes how people move, and movement changes business, memory, and landscape. Faster roads can connect places, but they can also cause people to pass by what they once noticed.
